questions.q: What is the main difference between the Enterprise WSDL and the Partner WSDL?
options: Enterprise WSDL is strongly typed to one org's current schema and must be regenerated when that schema changes; Partner WSDL is generic and loosely typed, working against any org without regeneration
Enterprise WSDL is for REST calls, and Partner WSDL is for SOAP calls
Partner WSDL only works for Partner-tier Salesforce editions
There is no real difference; both are generated identically for every org
questions.explain: Enterprise WSDL bakes in an org's specific custom objects and fields as typed classes, which breaks when the schema changes; Partner WSDL is generic and avoids that regeneration need.

questions.q: What does a successful SOAP `login()` call return?
options: A sessionId and a serverUrl, used on every subsequent SOAP call
An OAuth access token and a refresh token
Only a username confirmation, with no further values needed
A WSDL file
questions.explain: login() returns a sessionId (placed in a SessionHeader on later calls) and a serverUrl (the endpoint every later call is sent to).

questions.q: Which SOAP operation is used specifically to fetch the next batch of a query result that didn't fit in one response?
options: retrieve
describeSObjects
queryMore
upsert
questions.explain: queryMore continues a query whose full result set exceeded the batch size returned by the initial query call.

questions.q: Which SOAP operation inserts or updates a record based on an external ID field, rather than requiring you to already know the Salesforce record ID?
options: upsert
create
delete
query
questions.explain: upsert matches on an external ID field, inserting a new record if no match is found or updating the existing one if it is.

questions.q: According to this lesson, why does SOAP still matter even though REST is the default choice for new Salesforce integrations?
options: SOAP is actually faster than REST for every workload
Some enterprise middleware, older ETL tools, and legacy systems built years ago against Salesforce's SOAP API are still in production and rely on its strongly-typed WSDL contract
Salesforce requires every integration to use SOAP for authentication
REST cannot perform create, update, or delete operations
questions.explain: SOAP persists in real integration work mainly through legacy and enterprise systems that were built against it and depend on its formal, strongly-typed contract.
